situation:
You are the sales manager at PINE HOLLOW FAIR AND EXPOSITION COMPANY, which operates the county fairgrounds, its exhibit halls, its livestock arena and a recreational-vehicle campground. The general manager (judge), who arrived this year after two losing seasons, has asked you to recommend how one week of the spring calendar should be sold.

The county school district has proposed a partnership: a week-long student agriculture and robotics exposition every spring, using two exhibit halls and the campground, at a rate well below what those halls normally bring. The same week has been held for eleven years by commercial trade-show exhibitors, who pay far more per hall day and rebook it every fall. Only one of the two bookings can have the week.

The company's booking and ticket-scan records show that families who first come to the grounds for a school event return for the fair itself and reserve campground sites when they do. The campground sits close to half empty every spring, and the district's week would fill it. On paper the partnership is worth more over three years than the trade show is.

The sales staff, several of them with fifteen years on the grounds, disagree. They say student groups buy nothing on site, and that the displaced exhibitors will move to a competing fairground and not come back. The company can instead keep the week for those exhibitors, which leaves the campground close to half empty and gives up the returning families the records describe.

The general manager (judge) wants you to recommend which booking to sell, explain the selling process you would use, and name the direct marketing tactics that would carry it. You should also say which features of the grounds you would sell, what draws visitors to a fairground in the first place, and where the campground itself can be sold as lodging. The general manager (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager (judge) at PINE HOLLOW FAIR AND EXPOSITION COMPANY. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You were hired this year to return the fairgrounds to profit, and the spring calendar is the first thing you have asked the sales manager to rethink. You want to hear which of the two bookings should be sold that week, the selling process behind it, the direct marketing tactics that would support it, and how the campground would be sold as lodging alongside it.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Three years from now, what will this decision have changed about who comes to the grounds?
What could go wrong later that would not show up in the first season?
